ideas.pitch: A high-performance offline Python vectorised backtesting engine with regime-switching detection for simulated quantitative execution.
ideas.title: AlphaFlow Backtester
ideas.why_it_could_win: Judges in a quant trading hackathon heavily favor robust risk-adjusted returns and clean architecture over complex deep learning models that overfit historical data.

ideas.pitch: A sentiment-driven quantitative execution overlay that extracts sentiment indicators from financial news corpora to adjust algorithmic weights dynamically.
ideas.title: Sentiview Quant
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines natural language processing with traditional financial metrics, mirroring the pattern of multi-modal winning solutions from data science hackathons.

ideas.pitch: An automated portfolio allocation and dynamic stop-loss algorithmic wrapper designed to minimise maximum drawdown in volatile simulated markets.
ideas.title: RiskMatrix Portfolio Engine
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses strictly on risk management and capital preservation—metrics that quantitative hedge funds value above pure high-risk alpha generation.

ideas.pitch: A cointegration-based statistical arbitrage trading algorithm that executes automated mean-reversion trades across correlated asset pairs.
ideas.title: StatArb Pair Trading Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Implements a mathematically sound, classic quantitative finance strategy (Engle-Granger cointegration) that proves genuine domain intuition to judges.

ideas.pitch: A high-frequency tick-data analysis script that calculates order book imbalances to trigger micro-momentum execution signals.
ideas.title: OrderBook Imbalance Scalper
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core thesis of the hackathon that speed and structural edge matter in execution-heavy quantitative environments.
